_about: RATIFIED Company Standard — approved THROUGH THE LEGAL CONSTITUTION L1.10 §31.14, with the
owner's interpretation of 2026-09-14 recorded in AM-66: the two limbs are ONE compound
requirement and the notice limb is never evaluated alone. Every value is the section's own;
description: Planned discontinuation of a service gives advance notice and runs to the end of any committed term, whichever falls later.
source_document: Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.10 — docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.10.md
source_clause: §31.14 A. Planned Full Service Discontinuation / Retirement
source_quote: Provide 30 days' advance notice, OR continue the service until the customer's committed contract period ends, whichever is later.

evaluation_rules._note: presence is established by the mapping layer alone (45D); the evaluator reads no clause text

until the expiry of the committed term

_calibration: 2026-09-14 (AM-66): the compound position is expressed in TERMINOLOGY, not in a new evaluator — EvaluatorType is singular by locked 42.7/N-36 and no compound evaluator exists. Scored against the real mapper: the Constitution's own compound sentence = 7 (CONFIRMS -> MATCH); a one-limb clause 'may discontinue upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice' under a Discontinuation heading = 2 (below threshold, evidence retained -> UNRESOLVED -> Needs a decision); the same clause with no heading = 0; a non-payment discontinuation clause = -3 (vetoed, §31.14's own carve-out).
The heading terms are deliberately worth less than the threshold on their own, so a clause on the subject keeps its evidence and reaches a person rather than being asserted absent.
What is checked is that the CLAUSE provides the compound protection. LegalMind holds no contract dates, so it never computes the later of the two dates — a person does, from the clause it cites.
Limitation recorded: an unheaded one-limb clause scores 0 and produces no signal; it surfaces on the report as an unmatched provision (REC-02) rather than as a finding.

§31.14 B (material non-discontinuing change, 30 days 'where reasonably practicable') and C (six exceptions) are NOT measured by this standard — B's qualifier has no checkable boundary and C is a carve-out, not a position.

approval.ruling: owner, 2026-09-14: 'Treat the two conditions as one compound requirement: the required 30-day notice must be satisfied; and the committed contract term must have ended. The applicable discontinuation date is the later of these two dates. Do not evaluate the 30-day notice limb independently, because that would narrow the Constitution's actual meaning.'
